key_insight: Existing T2I evaluation (human ratings and preference-trained metrics) biases models toward overly vivid, oversaturated outputs; calibrating both benchmarks and model outputs for color fidelity yields generations that better match real-world photographic color distributions.
problem_solved: Addresses the mismatch where evaluation signals and model training encourage exaggerated saturation/contrast, causing 'too vivid to be real' images even under realism prompts and masking true color fidelity issues.
method: Construct a color-fidelity benchmark pairing real photographs with realism prompts and annotations that emphasize photographic color accuracy rather than subjective vividness.
Introduce objective color-fidelity measures (e.g., perceptual color distance and distribution divergence) and recalibrate preference-trained metrics to penalize unrealistic saturation/contrast.

Provide a calibration procedure (post-hoc score scaling or simple color-correction module) to adjust generative outputs or metric scores so model preferences align with photographic color distributions.
impact: Enables researchers and practitioners to reliably evaluate and tune generative models for photographic realism (not just visual vividness), reducing over-saturation artifacts and improving trustworthiness of T2I outputs in applications requiring authentic colors.
visual_elements: Before/after image triplets showing original prompt, over-vivid baseline output, and calibrated color-fidelity output
Scatter plot comparing human preference scores vs objective color-fidelity metric (illustrating bias toward vividness)
Pipeline diagram of benchmark → metric recalibration → model/post-process calibration
Color histogram or 2D chroma-lightness heatmaps comparing real photos vs generated images (pre- and post-calibration)
paper_title: Too Vivid to Be Real? Benchmarking and Calibrating Generative Color Fidelity
paper_authors: Zhengyao Fang, Zexi Jia, Yijia Zhong, Pengcheng Luo, Jinchao Zhang
